function.name: CloseLocal
function.description: Actually close ONE browser tab or ONE app window for a direct request. Pass the exact original Vietnamese command unchanged: "đóng tab Chrome", "đóng Notepad", "đóng ứng dụng hiện tại". Normal close only, never kill processes or discard save prompts. A tab request must never close the browser window: keep the last tab open. Only an explicit app/window close may close the whole window. No UI Plan or shell needed for this narrow tool. If the target is ambiguous, ask using its message. Do not retry or call another tool after an uncertain result; never claim success unless verified.

function.name: DeviceControl
function.description: Actually adjust laptop volume or screen brightness for a direct user request, including text typed in Bionic. Pass the original Vietnamese command unchanged, e.g. "âm lượng 40 phần trăm", "giảm 40 phần trăm âm lượng cho tôi", "độ sáng 70%", "tắt tiếng". Supports increase/decrease/set/read/mute/unmute and verifies the result. No UI Plan or shell is needed for this narrow control. Report only its verified result; never merely suggest taskbar/settings.

command.description: Exact current user command about laptop volume or brightness

function.name: MusicControl
function.description: Search and auto-play music on Spotify or YouTube, or pause/stop/resume/skip currently playing music. Pass the exact original Vietnamese command unchanged, e.g. "tìm kiếm nhạc Lạc Trôi", "phát bài Thiên Lý Ơi trên YouTube", "dừng nhạc đang chạy", "mở nhạc", "chuyển bài tiếp theo". No UI Plan or shell is needed for this narrow tool. Report only its verified result.

command.description: Exact current user command about searching, playing, or stopping music

function.name: OpenLocal
function.description: For a direct user request to open one app, file or folder, ACTUALLY open it now. If an app name is not installed but matches a configured or known website, open that website in the default browser instead of suggesting installation. Never edit files. If multiple file matches, ask which one. Minecraft opens TLauncher and presses Enter the game for the selected version; TLauncher alone opens only the launcher.

function.name: OpenWeb
function.description: For a direct user request to open a website or a URL they supplied, open it in the default browser now. Accept an exact http(s) URL, a configured site name, or a known website name. Do not search the web or claim that Browser Settings must be changed. Report only whether the browser accepted the address, not whether the page finished loading.

target.description: Exact URL or website name from the user request

function.name: FindLocal
function.description: Read-only: find an installed Windows app, configured website, local file, or folder by its name. Use for questions about where something is. If a requested app is not installed but a website of the same name exists, return its URL and call OpenWeb to fulfill an open request. For direct open requests prefer OpenLocal.

function.name: Plan
function.description: Call before multi-step computer UI actions. Set goal to the exact current user request, without adding instructions. A direct request to open one app, file or folder uses OpenLocal. Alex checks the scope automatically during the active turn; do not ask the user to approve it again. Supply specific absolute paths only when needed. Stop if denied.

function.name: Finish
function.description: End the approved plan after verifying the requested result. Quote exact evidence from the most recent Snapshot or read-only FileSystem result. A successful click/type alone is not task completion.

function.name: Cancel
function.description: Stop the plan and revoke further actions. Use on denial or when unable to finish.

function.name: App
function.description: Open/start/launch applications and manage windows. Keywords: open, start, launch, program, application, window, foreground, focus, resize. Four modes: 'launch' (opens an application by Start Menu name), 'launch_executable' (strictly launches one executable path with separated argv and optional cwd), 'resize' (adjusts a named or active window), and 'switch' (brings a specific window into focus).

function.name: PowerShell
function.description: Shell/command execution. Keywords: shell, run, execute, cmd, terminal, command line, script. A comprehensive system tool for executing any PowerShell commands. Use it to navigate the file system, manage files and processes, and execute system-level operations. Capable of accessing web content (e.g., via Invoke-WebRequest), interacting with network resources, and performing complex administrative tasks. This tool provides full access to the underlying operating system capabilities, making it the primary interface for system automation, scripting, and deep system interaction.

function.name: FileSystem
function.description: Manages file system operations with eight modes: 'read' (read text file contents with optional line offset/limit), 'write' (create or overwrite a file, set append=True to append), 'copy' (copy file or directory to destination), 'move' (move or rename file/directory), 'delete' (delete file or directory, set recursive=True for non-empty dirs), 'list' (list directory contents with optional pattern filter), 'search' (find files matching a glob pattern), 'info' (get file/directory metadata like size, dates, type). Relative paths are resolved from the user's Desktop folder. Use absolute paths to access other locations.

function.name: Snapshot
function.description: Take a screenshot and inspect the screen. Keywords: screenshot, screen capture, see screen, observe, look, inspect, UI elements, what's on screen. Captures complete desktop state including: system language, focused/opened windows, interactive elements (buttons, text fields, links, menus with coordinates), and scrollable areas. Set use_vision=True to include screenshot with cursor highlight. Set use_annotation=False to get a clean screenshot without bounding box overlays on UI elements (default: True, draws colored rectangles around detected elements). Set use_ui_tree=False for a faster screenshot-only snapshot when you do not need interactive or scrollable element extraction. Set width_reference_lines/height_reference_lines to overlay a grid for better spatial reasoning (make sure vision is enabled to use it). Set use_dom=True for browser content to get web page elements instead of browser UI. Set display=[0] or display=[0,1] using zero-based active Windows display indices; omit it to keep the default full-desktop behavior. Set region=[left, top, right, bottom] in virtual-desktop pixel coordinates to capture and inspect only that rectangle instead of the whole screen/display — useful when you already know which area matters and want to save tokens; region takes precedence over display when both are given, and an invalid or out-of-bounds region raises an error rather than silently capturing something else. Always call this first to understand the current desktop state before taking actions.

function.name: Click
function.description: Performs mouse clicks at specified coordinates [x, y] or passing a UI element's label/id. Supports button types: 'left' for selection/activation, 'right' for context menus, 'middle'. Supports clicks: 0=hover only (no click), 1=single click (select/focus), 2=double click (open/activate). Provide either loc or label.

function.name: Type
function.description: Types text at specified coordinates [x, y] or passing a UI element's label/id. Set clear=True to clear existing text first, False to append. Set press_enter=True to submit after typing. Set caret_position to 'start' (beginning), 'end' (end), or 'idle' (default). Provide either loc or label.

function.name: Scroll
function.description: Scrolls at coordinates [x, y], a UI element's label/id, or current mouse position if loc=None. Type: vertical (default) or horizontal. Direction: up/down for vertical, left/right for horizontal. wheel_times controls amount (1 wheel ≈ 3-5 lines). Use for navigating long content, lists, and web pages.

function.name: Move
function.description: Moves mouse cursor to coordinates [x, y] or passing a UI element's label/id. Set drag=True to perform a drag-and-drop operation from the current mouse position to the target coordinates, or provide from_loc=[x, y] to make the drag explicit-start and atomic in one tool call. Optional duration controls bounded intermediate movement. Default (drag=False) is a simple cursor move (hover). Provide either loc or label.

function.name: Shortcut
function.description: Executes keyboard shortcuts using key combinations separated by +. Examples: "ctrl+c" (copy), "ctrl+v" (paste), "alt+tab" (switch apps), "win+r" (Run dialog), "win" (Start menu), "ctrl+shift+esc" (Task Manager). Use for quick actions and system commands.
